title: GitHub Next Explorations: Rahul Pandita
talk_summary: A GitHub Next researcher describes their exploration process (prototype, dogfood internally, tech preview, product-or-kill) and demos two Copilot experiments: Next Edit Suggestions (multi-location edits beyond the cursor) and Copilot Workspace (issue → spec → plan → implementation with an editable, iterable, runnable environment). The talk is mostly product demo and process philosophy, with little measured data.

takeaways.technique: Spec → plan → implement as explicit editable stages
takeaways.what_they_do: Copilot Workspace turns an issue into a current-state spec, a target-state spec, then a file-level plan, then implementation; the user can edit any stage before proceeding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will tell you that these three files these three files need to be updated. And I will ... go ahead and implement it

takeaways.technique: Built-in runtime to verify AI output
takeaways.what_they_do: The workspace embeds a terminal and live preview so the user can immediately compile/run the generated change and see output, rather than trusting the diff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it has a built-in runtime that allows you to quickly verify what the the code that has been provided by the AI

takeaways.technique: Staged dogfooding gates with kill criteria
takeaways.what_they_do: Ideas pass through escalating gates (team dogfood → company dogfood → tech preview → product) and can be shelved at any point if signal is weak.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can kill or we can shelve any of these exploration at any point of time if we are not getting the right signal

takeaways.technique: Iterate/correct at any point instead of restarting
takeaways.what_they_do: Users can edit the spec, plan, or code mid-flight and re-run only the affected stage, keeping prior work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at any given point of time if you feel that something is not right, you can just go ahead and say that okay, add Rust

takeaways.what_they_do: Before planning, the system explicitly derives what the repo currently does and what it should do, grounding the plan in observed code rather than assumptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it just goes and figures out does the website have this playground ... And it goes to the target state
